own_solution.law: Doppler effect for sound in still air, applied twice: lorry panel as receding observer f1 = f(c-u)/c, then as receding source, recorder moving away from source along the propagation direction: f2 = f1(c-v)/(c+u). Shift = f[1 - (c-u)(c-v)/(c(c+u))] = f*7149/119707.
assumptions: ideal reflection with no frequency change in panel frame

defect_reasons.other: TBF04/TA0C8 change the emitted note around the time of pickup; strictly the reflected sound picked up just after a pitch change was emitted earlier at the old pitch, so the timing wording admits a transient reading, though the intended steady-state reading (note now 1910 Hz) is clear.

notes: Base: shift = 1500*7149/119707 = 89.581 Hz. With note 1910 Hz: 1910*7149/119707 = 114.067 Hz. The 82 m initial separation (TDC03/T6307) affects only arrival time, not the steady Doppler shift; I classify it D (it does not enter the frequency relations), though it is attached to the system geometry. TDC03 and T6307 state the same 82 m and differ only in 'stands' vs 'is'. T02E2/TBF04/T4BE2/TA0C8 all state 410 Hz and differ in attachment (earlier experiment, current note, violin). TA134 and TA6A4 state 'a further small amount' with no number; they are unquantified variants of the violin and earlier-experiment sentences and are D regardless of the amount. The busker/violin is structurally disconnected from the siren-lorry-recorder chain.
